venues.name: CC Atlanta
venues.narrative: **CCATL — Wednesday 8/19 (MOD: Mkz; entered by Mya)** Net sales $1,183 against a $1,507 target; food $250, no event sales. Comps $25.90. 43 guests at a $27.52 check average. Weather 92/71. Quiet Wednesday but great vibes regardless. The opener used the down time to knock out batches, and the team opened up a few new coupes — a reminder to take care of them. Finished the last of the Planteray rum today and replaced it with Bacardi, which can serve as well rum for now. No longer keeping the margarita batch in the middle well; added a bottle of Tito's to the middle well on both ends, which should help on the weekend. Overall very chill in both FOH and BOH — the focus now is prepping for the weekend. Kitchen: prep ahead to avoid any 86s. Maintenance: none. 86'd/low: 86 Banhez piña, low champagne lassi, low espresso martini mix, low menus, 86 white towels. No incidents or injuries; no-shows were not charged. Favorite moment: talking with regular Joe for a few hours — usually too busy when he comes in, so it was nice to finally get to know him.

venues.name: CC Nashville
venues.narrative: **CCNSH — Wednesday 8/19 (MOD/Chef: KK / JMS; entered by BC)** Net sales $592 against a $1,345 target — a significant miss. Food $22. Comps $7.40 / 1.25% (employee, industry). 18 guests at a $32.89 check average. Hot and sunny. Slower Wednesday night than usual; Fishmonger also reported being exceptionally slower than expected tonight. It is a back-to-school week, which probably contributed. The bar was under $300 at 7pm. Clay and BC used the time to complete additional side work and several deep-cleaning projects. Kitchen: John Michael held it down. Maintenance: kitchen prep sink dripping. 86'd: Miller High Life, Tanqueray. No incidents or injuries; no-shows were not charged. Favorite moment: a couple of old friends, Andrew and Mary, caught up in the bar for a few hours and were a delight to chat with — and it was good to put the quiet hours to use setting the room up for further success.

venues.name: D&C Denver
venues.narrative: **DVR — Wednesday 8/19 (AM: Maggie S, Evan, Lucas; PM: Maggie H)** AM/Marquee $1,400.88, D&C PM $8,075.27, total net sales $9,476.15 against a $9,482 target — essentially dead even before events. Add $9,098 in net event sales for $18,574.15 total. Food $2,754.40 plus $8,185 event food = $10,939.40. Comps $305.82. 254 guests (Tock). High 92 / low 62. AM notes: usual morning pop into a very mellow afternoon, quite a few IRDs; peach black and classic black tea need to be made tomorrow. Low: miso sesame, caramel. Out: kombucha, sparkling Saratoga, chocolate, miele, peach black. D&C notes: 5pm popped off and 7-8pm was fun, but the night was steady throughout. Garden: cocktail hour event for Xerocon, 25 guests 6-9pm — Lucas put out a nice buffet spread and a handful of apps and the group came with an appetite; Onya, Sam and Ryan breezed through, and the hosts were jovial and happy to have the redemption event on a beautiful August night. Events: day 2 of meetings for Anaconda LLC, 15 guests 8am-5pm in Vauxhall; Josh handled to-go breakfast and a lunch spread, the group worked straight through, day 3 tomorrow. Kitchen: pretty slow night with no real pops; Ayu did great on her first night; hefty prep list tomorrow. 911: mango curd, chantilly, quenelles, scallops, ranch, tarragon jam, pasta, cherry vermouth reduction, creamed spinach, steaks. 86: creamed spinach, scallops. Breaks made up; no incidents; no-shows not charged. Favorite moment: the last-minute 11pm pop.

venues.name: D&C East Village
venues.narrative: **EV — Wednesday 8/19 (MOD/Chef: Kyler & Steves; entered by Thomas)** Net sales $4,762 against a $4,386 target — comfortably over. Food $390, beverage $4,372. Comps $71.40. 120 guests at roughly a $40 check average. Warm. Service notes: after an extraordinarily slow first hour the room hit a solid flow state, including a busy 8-11pm. Food percentage was low (<10%, roughly a third of it from one large table), but the night carried some mega checks with several couples approaching or topping $200 — including a two-top of Australian finance guests. A gregarious crowd across the board. Back-catalog banger: Pixee Pícala, a softened, spiced Mezcal Negroni riff. 120 covers, 8 solos, 2 large parties. Top sellers: Cloudwalk, Native Lion, Rosalie/Burner Phone (tie). Door notes: warm but not too hot; a slow start relying on the steady 9pm post-dinner rush to fill the room, with a decent 8-9pm push of reservations creating a short waitlist for twos. Streets went quiet after 10:30pm, but Dave from Attaboy came in for a nightcap. Notable guests included Joseph Darragh celebrating an engagement, Eunice celebrating her niece's graduation, Koba unwinding after jury duty, and an Arizona bar manager celebrating her 21st with her parents, who nearly cried at the experience. Many first-time solo visitors with Death & Co at the top of their list. Ella had a great first night of training. No-shows: Daniel Levin (2 at 6:30pm), Will Crager (2 at 7:15pm) — not charged. Menu count 20; breakage 2 DOF, 1 footed pilsner.

venues.name: D&C Los Angeles
venues.narrative: **LA — Wednesday 8/19 (MOD/Chef: Julian and Saleh; entered by Julian Catano)** Net sales $6,134 against a $5,178 target — a strong beat. Food $1,265, all through Marquee; standing room and events at zero. Comps $315.50, driven by a few DNL returns and a handful of investors. 141 guests at a $43.51 check average. Warm and toasty. Started at a decent pace, picked up around 8pm and stayed consistent from there. Both servers stayed nearly to the end — Xavier left at last call and Angel stayed to close. Overall function was good with a few hiccups on food timing, but solid service throughout. Kitchen: 86 fries and cookies; a 20-minute wait on a dozen oysters, otherwise solid. Maintenance: loose tile — replacement tile has arrived. No incidents or injuries; no-shows were charged. Favorite moment: a young woman came in to celebrate her NP graduation and turned out to have friends in common with the team.

venues.name: D&C Washington DC
venues.narrative: **DC — Wednesday 8/19 (MOD: Marcus)** Marquee bar sales $4,087.29; total net sales including events $3,712.94 against a $4,247 target. Food $541.65; garden and event sales zero. Comps $70.25 (F&F $41.25, employee $29). 77 guests — 47 walk-ins, 30 reservations — at a $48.22 check average. Warm to start but cooled off to a pleasant night. Slow start, with the first pop around 6pm and most of the action at the bar top. With no nearby events driving traffic the outlook wasn't promising, so the host was cut around 8pm — then the room started to trickle in and by 9:45pm it was full. Devan handled the floor like a pro with an assist from Sasha, who put his server training to good use and earned glowing reviews. Jada and Ian rocked the bar top all night and both jumped onto the floor to run drinks and touch tables. Last call at 11:30pm, but guests hung out until 12:30am. Industry love included a visit from Khaleel, and Devon Tarby made an appearance. Kitchen: got hit later in the evening but James was ready. What went well: communication and everyone playing team player. What to improve: resetting to zero and always working to completion. Maintenance: garbage disposal. No injuries or incidents; no-shows not charged. Favorite moment: a line at the host stand on a Wednesday.

venues.name: Municipal Grand F&B
venues.narrative: **MG — Wednesday 8/19 (AM: Braden and Lex; PM: James and Marcus; entered by James)** Municipal Bar morning $535 (7 guests), evening $3,180 (77 guests), Sun Club $81, Hot Eye closed — total net sales $3,796 against a $4,500 target. Food $1,677. Comps $75. 84 guests at roughly a $45 check average. Hot. [Data note: the typed Total Net Sales field read $37,965, an evident keying error — the reported components sum to $3,796, which is what has been recorded here.] Morning: another quiet one, with Tia holding it down solo for hotel guests and the team from Pangea next door, who held a staff meeting over lunch. Brent worked hard in the back fixing leaks. Evening: a frustrating pace with no action until the sun was almost fully down — predictable at this point but not easier, with the team milling through small projects until the rush hour arrived. When it came, the bar filled and about nine tables of diners and drinkers were on. No service problems; Eva was a big help and stayed through the rush, and Tanner and Carla closed at a decent time. Jason managed the bar solo from open to close and did great on a long shift. Sun Club: nearly too hot for the roof, though Skylar had a few guests at the pool and some lingered after her bar shut down. Kitchen: smooth sailing, no notes. Maintenance: the AC unit is doing better but still dripping a puddle in front of the bar doors closest to the street. No injuries or incidents. Favorite moment: the little 9 o'clock pop that kept everyone awake and heads on a swivel.
